title: 1989 AHSME Problem 13
statement: Two strips of width \(1\) overlap at an angle of \(\alpha\) as shown. The area of the overlap (shown shaded) is

solutions.text:
The overlap is a parallelogram. Taking a slanted side as its base, the perpendicular height is the width \(1\) of the slanted strip. If that base has length \(L,\) its vertical component is the width of the horizontal strip, so \(L\sin\alpha=1.\) Hence \(L=\frac{1}{\sin\alpha},\) and the area is \(L\cdot1=\frac{1}{\sin\alpha}.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: The overlap is a parallelogram with altitude \(1\)
